messages.body_plain:
Hope the spring is treating you well.

I'm excited to do my workshop on sensitivity analysis (statistician's version) again this year with ICPSR.   Please circulate widely.

Ken

ICPSR <https://urldefense.com/v3/__https:/umich-dot-yamm-track.appspot.com/2hJP1gSBJYn-dMRD17B1dGdvcgCz29d3VXERAT3dTmFVJG7zonAF8cWSWoJ5tbOyVYO4nxhoUaIIGhikhWOgJRixV-4dpBOm9xL0We5BRZ1M6A4HlbWy0q40lcopKT2kxKwnE2_-s9NIE-gugJEeW5k4TgmOvzZwnBK68B7HXbfXqjFNdHFlkb--Oyw__;!!HXCxUKc!2Qzz3YzMloCNPF0oCY1ZmOtVlQ8jsGYZ4O-lg4-D-irlm2FhJu4zjqWwvF2sENiWo6rqrrU2l4iZ2sqcsrc$> course July 13, 2026 – July 17, 2026, 10:00 AM-3:00 PMET, virtual format

Sensitivity Analysis: Quantifying the Robustness of Inferences to Alternative Factors or Data <https://web.cvent.com/event/4ea180c8-1f25-4314-8da9-145297b14113/websitePage:17e8f24b-550c-4a09-a091-06ccd6f667d5?session=271f87c0-e192-4e2b-b873-c793487483b8&shareLink=true>.

Most social scientists need to consider the unobserved conditions that could change an inference. This workshop is about the statistical tools (R, Stata or the konfound-it app <https://konfound-project.shinyapps.io/konfound-it/>) to do just that, quantifying the strength of evidence to inform policy, practice, or general social science.

The course is 20 instruction hours -- half a semester's worth of instruction in just 5 days. That gives us time to tailor to specific examples or approaches in your field.
Register here. Group discounts available as well.
